newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan asks banks to bring down lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan asks banks to bring down lending rates.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Thursday it had asked banks to bring down the average lending rates for the corporate sector by slashing excessive and unnecessary overheads.

"We have asked all banks that they should reduce their costs in all areas and pass on the benefit to borrowers and depositors through lower lending rates and higher rate of return on deposits," SBP Governor Muhammad Yaqub told reporters.
He said lending rates for the corporate sector averaged 17.5 percent with the rates of return on deposits ranging from seven to eight percent.
The consumer price index for April was at 13.57 percent compared to 11.03 in April 1996, official figures show.

"Most of the nationalised (state-owned) banks have a high non-performing loan portfolio with financial intermediation cost at above five percent compared to two to three percent around the world," Yaqub said.

He said Pakistan's banking system had a total bad debt portfolio of 127 billion stuck up mostly with 3,724 insolvent or near-insolvent industrial units, with the share state-run banks and financial institutions coming to 92 billion rupees.
The SBP also announced Thursday it had offered a scheme of inventives to loan defaulters to encourage settlement and recovery of bad debts.
